claims.text: The feedstock is AlCrFeNiSi alloy powder intended for additive manufacturing.
A closed-loop machine-learning system can dynamically adjust laser energy density and scan strategy during the build.
Machine-learning-guided low-thermal-load processing can mitigate residual thermal stresses in miniature AlCrFeNiSi components.
Machine-learning-guided low-thermal-load processing can improve the mechanical properties of miniature AlCrFeNiSi components.
The proposed intervention can simplify additive-manufacturing processing relative to conventional high-energy methods.
A low-thermal-load processing window is applicable to miniature AlCrFeNiSi component geometries.
The intervention will reduce thermal gradients and refine the microstructure.
Reduced thermal gradients and a refined microstructure will lower residual-stress accumulation and minimize crack-initiation sites.
The ML system will use real-time sensor feedback and pre-trained models to control processing.
Dynamic process-parameter adjustment can prevent excessive local energy input.
Rapid solidification in laser powder-bed processing induces thermal stresses in high-entropy alloys.
Avoiding excessive local energy input will produce a more uniform and mechanically robust microstructure.
Components made with the proposed process will have lower residual stress than components made under conventional high-thermal-load conditions.
Components made with the proposed process will have better tensile performance than conventionally produced components.
Components made with the proposed process will have better fatigue performance than conventionally produced components.
Components made with the proposed process will require less post-processing than conventionally produced components.
Conventional high-energy additive manufacturing produces rapid melting and solidification, high thermal gradients, substantial residual stresses, and complex post-processing requirements.
The magnitude of stress reduction and mechanical-property improvement depends on ML-model accuracy and sensor-feedback consistency.
Performance may vary across alloy-powder batches and component geometries.
